smells.finding: checks.py's refs_line_self_consistent grew from a shape+legend+arithmetic check to a shape+legend+TEST_NOTE+arithmetic check: ~67 lines of code (excluding its own docstring), now bundling 4 distinct concerns in one function -- header shape (exactly one production + one tests line), legend-follows check, TEST_NOTE presence/absence, and ~8 per-line arithmetic invariants. This is a real, if moderate, growth in both size and concern-count, not merely a proportional restatement of what was there before. Not blocking -- the function remains a single coherent PAGE-LOCAL pass over one page's parsed lines (the docstring's own stated locality goal: avoid re-reading the page per concern), and every added concern is a natural extension of the SAME self-consistency invariant this function already owned. Worth a future split (header-shape vs. per-line arithmetic) if it grows again.
No classes added or grown by this diff. checks.py's MapUnderCheck/StoreScan/SourceScan are untouched (confirmed: no hunk in the diff touches their line ranges).

render.py's REFS_PROD_PREFIX/REFS_TEST_PREFIX/TEST_NOTE/SPLIT_LEGEND and checks.py's byte-identical copies of the same four constants (plus is_test_module, declared twice) look like textbook duplication.

override.repo_standard: scripts/code_map/checks.py's own established, repeatedly-applied convention (already present for REFS_LEGEND and REFS_PREFIX before this gate; g3/g4's reviews already overrode the same pattern for their own gates) -- checks.py's module docstring and each duplicated constant's own comment state the rule explicitly: 'declared here, not imported from the renderer... a check that reads its expected text out of the code under test can only ever agree with it.' This is also CREW_CONTEXT.md's 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it' verification-discipline rule applied at the constant/predicate level, not just the assertion level.
override.reason: The duplication is the load-bearing mechanism, not an accident: it is what let this review's own independence-divergence attack (mutating ONLY checks.py's copy of is_test_module) prove the second copy actually catches a renderer/checker disagreement -- inbound_attribution and refs_line_self_consistent both went red. An imported single copy could never fail that way. The repo standard specifically subordinates this smell for exactly this class of verification code.

The pre-existing Refs namedtuple (sites, modules, named, own) is unchanged in shape; the new by_prefix dict in inbound_attribution groups two Refs under their own named prefix keys rather than passing an unlabeled tuple around. No new parameter clump introduced.
REFS_PROD_PREFIX/REFS_TEST_PREFIX are bare strings, consistent with the pre-existing REFS_PREFIX convention this file already used before this gate -- a carried-forward pattern, not a new instance.

Every new/changed function signature stays short: _bucket_line(prefix, counter, mod) [3], refs_line(key, mod) [2, unchanged], is_test_module(mod) [1], refs_prefix_of(line) [1]. No growth of an existing signature in this diff.

The whole diff is one cohesive feature (the production/test split) touching exactly the three files a single feature of this shape would touch (renderer, its checks, its tests) -- not a change rippling across many unrelated call sites for one small edit.

render.py changes for one reason (rendering the two-bucket split); checks.py changes for one reason (verifying it, plus tc32's ordering falsifier which reuses the same _bucket_line refactor). Confirmed by reading the diff hunks directly, not the hunk headers -- no file mixes two unrelated reasons to change.
truth.get(own_module, 0), counter.get(mod, 0), by_prefix[refs_prefix_of(line)] are single-level lookups at their call sites, not chained navigation through multiple objects.

_bucket_line is shared by exactly two concrete callers (production and test buckets) inside the SAME function that calls it twice -- exercised immediately, not spare capacity for an imagined third bucket. No unused hook, no stub, no ignored parameter anywhere in the diff.

Docstrings state design decisions and their reasoning throughout (is_test_module explains why it reads the dotted name rather than the file path and why it is a second hand-written copy; _bucket_line explains why there is exactly one sorted() call in the file; refs_line explains what splitting the total into two buckets buys a reader).
